exam_metadata.title: Getting Started — Question Types
exam_metadata.description: One question of every supported type. Each one explains itself while being an example of what it describes.

content.text:
Welcome

This source holds one question of every type the app supports. Work through it once and you will have seen everything a JSON file can contain.

The eight types

  • reading and topic_review — prose cards with no answer. You read them and rate how well you knew the material.
  • single_choice, multiple_choice, true_false — options with one or more marked correct.
  • short_answer — you type the answer and it is compared to a list of accepted spellings.
  • fill_in_the_blank — the answer sits inside the sentence.
  • flashcard — a front and a back; you rate yourself instead of being graded.

Open any question in the editor to see how it is built, then use this file as a template for your own.

answer.explanation: Reading cards carry no answer. They exist to be read before you test yourself on the material.

content.text: What is the animal in the photograph eating?

answer.explanation: Giant pandas eat almost nothing but bamboo. This question also shows how to attach an image: put a media entry on the content and set position to above or below.

content.text: Which question types need an options list?

answer.explanation: Only the three choice types use options. A multiple_choice question must have at least two options marked correct — mark just one and the app will tell you the question contradicts its own type.

content.text: A true_false question may have a third option.
Which city is the capital of Turkey?

answer.explanation: List every spelling you are willing to accept. Matching ignores case and surrounding spaces unless you set caseSensitive to true.

content.text: HTTP uses port {{80}}, HTTPS uses port {{443}}, and DNS uses port {{53|Port 53}}.

answer.explanation: The answers live inside the sentence in double braces, so there is no accepted_texts list to keep in sync. A pipe adds alternative spellings: the first one is shown as the correct answer, the rest are simply accepted.

content.text: What makes a flashcard different from every other question type?

answer.back: Nothing is graded. You reveal the back, judge yourself with Again / Hard / Normal / Easy, and that rating decides when the card comes back.

content.text:
Field reference

Only id, type and the question text are required. Everything below is optional — this file leaves several of them out on purpose so you can see what a minimal question looks like.

  • category — a label for grouping
  • tags — an array of strings, searchable and filterable
  • difficulty — 1 to 5, feeds the scheduling algorithm
  • starred / flagged — the two markers shown above the question
  • answer.explanation — shown after checking, on every type
  • content.media — an image or video, positioned above or below the text

Answers by type

  • choice types → answer.correct_ids
  • short_answer → answer.accepted_texts
  • fill_in_the_blank → {{markers}} in the text itself
  • flashcard → answer.back
  • reading / topic_review → no answer at all

answer.explanation: Keep this card flagged while you write your first file, then unflag it once the schema is familiar.
